title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: Major — if universal, false; revealed qualities/acts ≠ formal decree
pass_a_gloss: These things having been premised I come to the reason proposed, and I say that the Major, whose truth they cry out to be manifest, is either manifestly false, or particular, and then from all particulars the conclusion will be inept. If the Major be universal, in this manner, Any will of God whatsoever concerning the salvation and ruin of men revealed in the Gospel is the whole and entire decree of predestination, it is manifestly false. For God has revealed his will as to the qualities with which all who will be partakers of eternal life ought to be endowed; he has revealed his will as to the acts which ought to be exercised by all who will to enter eternal life; yet in these as it were statutes revealed to the human race the formal decree of the Divine predestination is not contained; but in that secret intention or will of efficaciously and infallibly gifting to certain elect those qualities, those acts, which lead to eternal life, and eternal life itself.
pass_b_english: With that premised I turn to their reason. The Major they call self-evident is either manifestly false, or particular — and then from particulars the conclusion is inept. If universal — Any gospel-revealed will of God about men's salvation and ruin is the whole entire decree of predestination — it is manifestly false. God has revealed his will about the qualities all who will share eternal life must have, and about the acts all who will enter that life must exercise; yet those revealed statutes do not contain the formal decree of divine predestination. That lies in the secret intention or will to gift certain elect efficaciously and infallibly those qualities and acts that lead to eternal life, and eternal life itself.
source_text: Hisce praemissis accedo ad rationem propositam, ac dico Majorem, cujus illi veritatem manifestam esse clamant, aut manifeste falsam esse, aut particularem, atque tum ex omnibus particularibus inepta erit conclusio. Si Major universalis sit, hoc modo, Quaelibet Dei voluntas de salute et exitio hominum in Evangelio patefacta, est totum et integrum decretum praedestinationis, manifeste falsa est. Deus enim revelavit voluntatem suam quoad qualitates quibus praediti debent esse omnes qui futuri sunt aeternae vitae participes; revelavit voluntatem suam quoad actus, qui exerceri debent ab omnibus, qui ingredi volunt vitam aeternam; hisce tamen quasi statutis humano generi revelatis, non continetur formale decretum praedestinationis Divinae; sed in illa arcana intentione sive voluntate efficaciter et infallibiliter donandi electis quibusdam illas qualitates, eos actus, qui ducunt ad vitam aeternam, ipsamque vitam aeternam.
